title: Don’t blame Europe’s riots on immigration
gist: Andrew Adonis argues the October 2026 riots in Paris, Milan and other European cities resemble England 2011 (spontaneous cost-of-living and schooling discontent), not race riots or revolution, and that stagnation, not collapse, is the real challenge.

insights.claim: The recent riots in Paris, Milan and other European cities look like the England 2011 model of spontaneous discontent followed by looting and copycat disorder, not France 1968 or a revolution.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Lowers odds of regime-threatening instability; unrest is a policy signal, not a systemic break.
insights.quote: It looks as if the violent outbreaks in Paris, Milan and a few other European cities are on the model of England 2011

insights.claim: The triggers were economic and institutional: Paris protests began in middle-class arrondissements over dilapidated schools, and Italy's over cost of living, with truckers and farmers blockading the port of Naples.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Cost-of-living pressure is the driver; watch logistics chokepoints in southern Italy.

insights.claim: The disturbances do not appear to be race riots, contradicting Donald Trump and far-right commentators who blame mass migration.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Immigration-blame narratives may mislead on the actual political-risk driver.
insights.quote: none of the recent disturbances appear to have been race riots or race-inspired

insights.claim: Populists of left and right in France, Italy, Germany and elsewhere do not command armed vigilantes as in the 1930s; Le Pen and Mélenchon are rabble rousers, not violent revolutionaries.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Tail risk of extra-constitutional political change in Europe is low.
insights.locator: As for concern about the rise of populist extremism

insights.claim: Le Pen's post-riot speech was essentially the same appeal for order and police support as Macron's, differing mainly in blaming the incumbent for weakness and exhaustion.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Mainstream convergence on law and order limits near-term polarisation.

insights.claim: Giorgia Meloni, a populist-right head of government, operates within conventional conservative democratic norms and recently gave a major speech backing Zelensky and a free European Union, in effect opposing Trump, Putin and the French and German far right.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Italy remains a pro-Ukraine, pro-EU anchor despite its populist label.

insights.claim: European leaders (Meloni, Macron, Merz, Burnham) lack a prosperity agenda, and AI threatens even current prosperity, particularly for the young and the poor.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Youth and low-income economic stress plus AI disruption is a persistent source of European political risk.
insights.locator: The problem for Meloni and Macron

insights.claim: Closing borders to immigrants is the closest quick fix leaders have and is happening country by country, but it leaves open what happens when growth does not follow.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Border tightening without growth may leave discontent unaddressed.
insights.quote: But when the borders close to outsiders and growth doesn’t follow, what then?
insights.locator: The problem for Meloni and Macron

insights.claim: German industrial production fell by more than half between 1929 and 1932 but only about nine per cent since 2018, marking today's stagnation as categorically different from catastrophic meltdown.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Useful base rate: the current downturn is chronic decline, not collapse.

insights.claim: Adonis's priorities are stopping Russia inflicting more war on Europe, civilising AI, and boosting European services, industry, education and training; the riots are a call to action rather than cause for alarm.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Signals the policy agenda centrist European elites are likely to prioritise.
insights.quote: This is all doable, just don’t panic.
